title: Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services Compliance Note: The Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage
content:
The compliance office's rule on the Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage (ABN, form CMS-R-131) for **Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services**.

## Rule

> Before a Part B therapy service Medicare is expected to deny as not reasonable and necessary is furnished at the resident's wish, the Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage is delivered and the beneficiary checks one of its options; the choice is the beneficiary's and is recorded as checked. Without a valid ABN, the resident is never billed for a denied service. The ABN is not used for services Medicare never covers or for tiers other than Part B. One notice is recorded per delivery date and first service described.

The notice applies in the Medicare Part B Physical Therapy Plan of Care, the Medicare Part B Occupational Therapy Plan of Care and the Medicare Part B Speech-Language Pathology Plan of Care. Its options are Option 1 (bill Medicare), Option 2 (do not bill) and Option 3 (decline the service).

## What a recorded notice shows

The option the beneficiary checked, the first service the notice describes, and the delivery date. One notice is recorded per delivery date and first service described.

## Basis Q&A

**When is the ABN delivered?** Before a Part B therapy service that Medicare is expected to deny as not reasonable and necessary is furnished at the resident's wish.

**Who chooses the option?** The beneficiary. The choice is the beneficiary's, and it is recorded as checked.

**Can the resident be billed for a denied service without a valid ABN?** No. Without a valid ABN, the resident is never billed for a denied service.

**Is the ABN used for a service Medicare never covers?** No.

**Is the ABN used for a Medicare Advantage, Medical Assistance or private-pay plan of care?** No. It is not used for tiers other than Part B.

## Hypothetical cases

| Hypothetical case | Reading |
|---|---|
| A Part B physical therapy service Medicare is expected to deny as not reasonable and necessary; the resident wishes to receive it | The ABN is delivered before the service is furnished, and the beneficiary checks one of its options |
| The same service was furnished and denied; no valid ABN exists | The resident is not billed for it |
| A Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care visit | The ABN is not used |
| Two notices delivered on different dates describing the same first service | Each is recorded on its own delivery date |
